h1: The 6 Best Worx Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Worx Leaf Blowers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six Worx leaf blowers, cordless and Trivac 3-in-1, compared on airflow in CFM, format and price range so you can match yard size.
summary: The 780 CFM cordless Worx is the best of the line, with the highest airflow here in the $100 to $200 range. The Trivac 3-in-1 adds vacuum and mulching at 600 CFM for less, though it needs a cord. The 530, 410 and 360 CFM cordless models step down in power, and the 340 CFM backpack ranks last.
intro: Worx sells half a dozen leaf blowers under almost the same name, which is a gift to anyone who likes a confusing shopping trip. The titles say cordless leaf blower, the photos look alike, and the only honest separator is airflow in CFM. Here it runs from 340 to 780 across the line, more than double, and price barely tracks it.

That makes this a CFM ranking first and a feature ranking second. We placed six Worx blowers using the airflow, power type and format each listing states, along with its price range. These are spec-sheet judgments, so battery capacity and run time, which the listings leave out, need checking before you buy. Where names collide, we separate the models by their airflow figure.

products.name: Worx Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The 780 CFM cordless is the most powerful Worx blower in this ranking.
products.description:
The 780 CFM cordless is the Worx to buy, because airflow is the one number that tells you how much leaf-covered ground a blower can move. At 780 CFM it leads the line by a wide margin, and it sits in the $100 to $200 range, the same bracket as models with half the power. Volume of air is what lifts wet, matted leaves instead of just rolling the dry ones.

It ranks first over the 530 CFM model because it gives roughly 250 more CFM at the same price, which is a difference you notice on a damp lawn. The Trivac adds functions, but not this power.

Buy it for larger yards and heavy leaf cleanup. The caveat is information: the listing does not give battery or run-time details, and a cordless blower at this airflow can drain a small pack quickly, so check the battery before ordering.
pros: Same price range as weaker models
products.idealFor: Larger yards and heavy leaf cleanup.
products.skipIf: You only have a small patio.

products.name: WORX Trivac 3-in-1 Electric Leaf Blower/Leaf Vacuum/Leaf Mulcher
products.verdict: Blows, vacuums and mulches at 600 CFM for $50 to $100.
products.description:
The Trivac is the odd one: an electric 3-in-1 that blows, vacuums and mulches, with 600 CFM of airflow at $50 to $100. Mulching shreds leaves into a fraction of their volume, which matters at the end of the job when you are staring at bags. It is the only Worx here that tackles disposal as well as movement.

It ranks second because it beats the 530 CFM cordless on airflow and price, but gives up the freedom of no cord. Against the 780 CFM leader, it trails by 180 CFM and requires an outlet and extension cord.

Choose it if you want to mulch leaves while clearing them and an outlet is close. The caveat is bulk: the vacuum and mulch parts make it larger to store than a handheld, and the cord limits how far from the house you can work.
products.idealFor: Gardeners who want to mulch leaves.

products.name: WORX Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 530 CFM cordless for mid-sized yards.
products.description:
This 530 CFM cordless is the model that gets squeezed. It lists 530 CFM of airflow, runs without a cord and lands in the $100 to $200 range. That is plenty for a mid-sized yard with light to moderate leaf fall, and cordless operation keeps setup simple.

It ranks third because the 780 CFM model costs the same and moves about half again as much air, while the Trivac adds vacuum and mulching for less money. The 530 still beats the 410 CFM unit below it on airflow at the same price.

Buy it for a mid-sized yard if you can find it at a good price, ideally below its stronger sibling. The caveat is value: at an identical bracket, you leave airflow on the table, so compare the 780 CFM listing first. Battery details are not listed either.
products.skipIf: A stronger model costs the same.

products.name: WORX Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 410 CFM cordless for tidy small and mid-sized lawns.
products.description:
The 410 CFM cordless is the light-duty version. It lists 410 CFM, no cord and a $100 to $200 range. That airflow handles dry leaves on tidy lawns and keeps patios and driveways clear.

It ranks fourth because it offers less airflow than the 530 and 780 CFM models at the same price, a poor trade when the stronger machines cost no more. It does edge out the 360 CFM unit below, but the price gap there is what matters: that one saves you a bracket of spending.

Choose it only for light cleanup on tidy lawns where heavy or wet leaves are rare. The caveat is that mid-low airflow struggles with damp piles. Before buying, compare the 530 CFM model, and look at the 360 CFM if the aim is simply to save money.
products.skipIf: You want the best airflow per dollar.

products.name: WORX Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: The cheaper 360 CFM cordless for decks and small yards.
products.description:
The 360 CFM cordless is the budget answer. It lists 360 CFM, cordless operation and a $50 to $100 range, making it the least expensive cordless Worx here. For a deck, driveway or small yard, 360 CFM is enough to push dry leaves and light debris without any cord.

It ranks fifth because airflow trails every model above it. The price gap is its selling point: next to the 410 CFM model, which costs in the $100 to $200 range, it saves a bracket while giving up only about 50 CFM.

Buy it for hard surfaces and small spaces. The caveat is capacity, as it is the weakest cordless airflow in the line and will struggle with wet leaves or a large lawn. Skip it if your property has big trees, and check the battery details on the listing, since none are given.

products.name: WORX Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 340 CFM backpack-format blower for longer sessions.
products.description:
The backpack Worx is the outlier in both directions. It lists 340 CFM in a backpack format and sits in the $200 to $500 range, the highest price in the line. Moving the weight to your back is a real advantage over long sessions, since a handheld hangs from one arm for the whole job.

It ranks last because it has the lowest airflow here at the highest price. The backpack format is its only differentiator, and the handheld Worx models give far more air, up to 780 CFM, for less money.

Buy it only if carrying the weight on your back matters more than raw power, perhaps for a long job and a shoulder problem. The caveat is plain: for most yards a handheld gives more airflow for less, so verify what you are paying for.
products.idealFor: Long cleanup sessions on your feet.
products.skipIf: You want the most airflow for the money.

whatMatters.detail: CFM is cubic feet per minute, the volume of air a blower moves. Higher CFM clears more leaves at once and lifts wet ones that low airflow just slides across the ground. Find the figure in the listing title or bullets, since several Worx models share a name. Here it runs from 340 to 780, which is the number that separates them.

Cordless blowers run on a battery, so there is no cord to drag, but runtime is limited and capacity varies. Electric models run as long as you like but need an outlet and an extension cord. Decide by yard size and outlet distance from the house, and check the battery details on the listing, since several here omit them.

A 3-in-1 unit can blow, vacuum and mulch leaves. Mulching shreds them into a fraction of the volume, so you fill fewer bags and make fewer trips to the curb. On the listing, confirm that the functions are named and that the attachments and collection bag are included, since a blower-only part count looks similar in photos.

Handheld blowers are lighter to store and cheaper, while backpack blowers move the weight to your back for long sessions. The better choice depends on how long you work at once. Check the listing for the format, and note that the backpack here has lower airflow than the handhelds.

Worx units here run from $50 to $500, and a higher price range does not always mean more airflow. The backpack costs the most and moves the least air of the six. Compare CFM first, then price, and always look for models in the same bracket where the stronger one is simply the better buy.

faq.q: Why do several Worx blowers have the same name?
faq.a: Worx reuses the name across models, so the titles look alike on the shelf and in search results. The CFM figure and the listing number are what separate the 780, 530, 410 and 360 CFM cordless models.

faq.q: What is the biggest buying mistake?
faq.a: Buying by name rather than CFM. Airflow in this line runs from 340 to 780 CFM, and the 780 CFM cordless costs the same as the 410 and 530 CFM models, so paying the same for less air is the real error.

faq.q: Is the Trivac worth it over a cordless model?
faq.a: If you want to mulch leaves, yes. It lists 600 CFM at $50 to $100, but it is electric and needs an outlet and extension cord, unlike the cordless models. Skip it if you hate cords.

faq.q: Which blower is best for a small deck?
faq.a: The 360 CFM cordless is enough for decks and driveways and is the cheapest cordless here. The Trivac also works if an outlet is close, and it adds vacuum and mulching for a bit more airflow.

faq.q: How do I check battery details?
faq.a: Our data does not list battery specs for these models, so read each listing carefully before buying. Look for voltage and amp hours, and check whether a battery and charger are included in the box, because that changes the real cost.

faq.q: Why is the backpack blower ranked last?
faq.a: The backpack blower has the lowest airflow at 340 CFM and the highest price range, $200 to $500. Its only edge is carrying weight on your back during long sessions, which rarely outweighs the weaker airflow.

finalTake: Buy the 780 CFM cordless for larger yards and wet leaves, or the Trivac if mulching appeals and an outlet is near. The 530 CFM model only makes sense if it undercuts its stronger sibling. The 360 CFM is the budget deck blower, and the backpack gives up too much airflow for its price.
